families.name: The Tall Woman Beyond the Trees
families.identity: An impossibly tall, pale figure with a broad dark hat; her face never resolves. An original tall-woman apparition, using modern folklore imagery without claiming to reproduce a particular tradition.
families.constraint: Needs long vertical sightlines, partial trunk occlusion, and a quiet previous minute. Her height is noticed gradually; she never becomes a fully lit close-up model.

families.name: The Voice Wearing Someone Else
families.identity: An unseen mimic repeats familiar voices with wrong timing, direction, or phrasing. It never proves that a real worker or dog has been replaced.
families.constraint: Requires actual recorded/legally usable in-game voice material or clearly synthesized original lines. Select only known voices and respect speaker locations.

families.name: The Antlered Wing
families.identity: A large winged outline with branching horn-like shapes, inspired by the visual language of woodland cryptids. It is mostly sound, shadow, and interrupted sky.
families.constraint: Best on windy ridges, open camp sky, and remote rock-camera views; avoid repeated flyovers or a readable creature turnaround.

families.name: The Low White Shape
families.identity: A crawling, pale form whose limbs are never fully countable. It uses low sightlines, roots, and spaces beneath structures rather than conventional standing silhouettes.
families.constraint: Requires actual ground occlusion and a valid travel path outside safety. Very brief rapid movement is rare and never becomes a repeated chase minigame.

families.name: The Faceless Surveyor
families.identity: A thin, motionless human outline positioned as if measuring your progress. Its missing facial detail comes from distance and obscurity, never an exposed blank-face close-up.
families.constraint: Uses long sightlines and persistent sighting memory. Appearances are separated by quiet work, not a teleport every time the player blinks.

families.name: The Worker Who Never Came Back
families.identity: A distant worker-like silhouette repeats the end of a shift after the real crew has returned. It exploits familiar routines without changing actual employment state.
families.constraint: Requires at least one established worker; before hiring, substitute a clearly unknown distant logger silhouette and avoid claiming someone is missing.

families.name: The Guest at the Window
families.identity: The impression of someone looking in, delivered through glass, curtains, reflections, and uncertain sightlines. It never becomes a physical camper intruder.
families.constraint: Needs a window with coherent reflection and outside geometry. A near-window surprise is one of the few eligible nonlethal jumpscare categories.

families.name: The Knocking Rule
families.identity: A repeating rhythm turns ordinary building sounds into apparent communication. The game never secretly requires a ritual response to survive.
families.constraint: Select one short rhythm per night and develop it across locations with long gaps. Do not teach a false mandatory superstition or disable sleep.

families.name: The Backward Walker
families.identity: A distant person-like shape travels with an unsettling gait and orientation. Natural occlusion hides its mechanics; it never moonwalks comically across a brightly lit yard.
families.constraint: Needs a moderate distance and partial lower-body visibility. Use short authored movement segments aligned to terrain.

families.name: The Dog That Is Not Your Dog
families.identity: Familiar canine sounds and incomplete distant shapes contradict the real dog's safe location. The real companion is never replaced, injured, or removed.
families.constraint: Activate after the player has learned the dog's voice and routines; always retain the actual dog in a coherent inspectable state.

families.name: The Drowned Walker
families.identity: Water sounds and a soaked distant silhouette move where no one should be wading. The horror depends on the island's ponds, river, and shoreline.
families.constraint: Needs mapped water depth, reachable banks, and accurate shore acoustics; no new lethal water rule or teleporting the player into water.

families.name: The Lantern Procession
families.identity: Small moving lights suggest a group taking a route that no living crew uses. Their spacing, silence, and changing count create dread.
families.constraint: Requires distant dark paths and no confusion with actual required safety lights. Apparent lanterns never protect the player.

families.name: The Boundary That Seems to Move
families.identity: Distance and familiar landmarks feel wrong through attention, fog, lighting, and sound. Navigation stays fair and the actual camp never secretly relocates.
families.constraint: Use authored visual/audio ambiguity rather than rewriting terrain or blocking the return path. Disable the effect when route assistance is needed.

families.name: The Hanging Shadows
families.identity: Long, suspended shadow shapes resemble coats, branches, or motionless bodies without depicting gore. Nothing becomes a collectible corpse or required investigation.
families.constraint: Needs canopy or roof occlusion and subtle wind variation; keep shapes partly hidden, with no close anatomical reveal.

families.name: The Camera Audience
families.identity: Something appears aware of observation without using cheap fourth-wall account access. It responds to in-game cameras, not the user's real webcam.
families.constraint: Requires an active watched feed and a clear separation between camera attention and the player's physical safety. Do not request device camera/microphone access.

families.name: The Room That Loses Its Warmth
families.identity: The feeling of refuge becomes emotionally fragile through sound, color, and ordinary objects, while its physical safety remains absolute.
families.constraint: Interior/camp atmospheric sequence with bounded grading and audio; never disable safety lamps or invent a temperature-survival meter.

families.name: The Choir in the Dead Air
families.identity: Natural sound almost forms voices, then withdraws before becoming a comprehensible explanation. Silence is part of the event, not constant ominous music.
families.constraint: Needs low recent sound intensity and a specific spatial source cluster. Captions describe ambiguous distant vocal-like sound without asserting a real speaker.

families.name: The Axe Beneath the Ground
families.identity: Logging sounds occur in impossible or abandoned places. It makes the player's comforting work rhythm feel borrowed by something unseen.
families.constraint: Reuses licensed/original work sounds with deliberate spatial/material changes. Never awards phantom felling money or damages unseen original trees.

families.name: The Room That Sounds Occupied
families.identity: An unseen routine seems to continue in an empty adjacent space. Actual interiors, workers, and bed assignments stay consistent.
families.constraint: Requires a real adjacent porch, bathroom exterior, storage space, or window occlusion. No fake permanent room or geometry traps.

families.name: The Afterimage on the Trail
families.identity: Attention and motion leave a fleeting human-like impression. Use authored silhouettes and occlusion rather than forced screen flashes or effects that depend on eye tracking.
families.constraint: Reads camera orientation and recent glance history only; no access to eyes or real biometric information. Comfort settings can soften all transitions.

families.name: The Uninvited Fifth
families.identity: An apparent extra person unsettles a group without changing the actual roster. The count adapts to however many workers really exist.
families.constraint: Requires at least one established companion and a verified real headcount. Never create an inaccessible extra bed or force repeated counting chores.

families.name: The Bell That Finds You
families.identity: A small bell-like tone appears to choose the player's route. Its timbre and spacing evolve without becoming a constant directional enemy alarm.
families.constraint: Needs low event intensity and good positional sound. Keep distinct from the real dog's collar and any UI alert.

families.name: The Patch Without Stars
families.identity: A bounded dark presence interrupts the sky or distant background. It creates scale anxiety without turning the whole game black.
families.constraint: Needs a readable night sky and safe contrast. No photosensitive flashes, forced darkness over UI, or disappearance of safety lamps.

families.name: The Red Thread
families.identity: Small ribbon-like markers suggest someone has been following the player's work. They are original temporary horror props, not an asserted cultural ritual.
families.constraint: May place removable cosmetic props only in unobserved valid locations. They never become completion targets, tripwires, or mandatory superstition tasks.

families.name: The Live Feed That Lies
families.identity: Rare, deliberately authored image anomalies challenge trust in the monitor while the underlying camera system remains genuinely live.
families.constraint: Late-unlocked family with explicit horror-layer implementation and diagnostics. Never hide ordinary bugs as paranormal effects or alter genuine saves, clocks, or user files.

families.name: The Night the Dog Runs
families.identity: One rare major rescue set piece: an exterior wind-roar forces the camper door open and the unharmed dog bolts toward a reachable trail. This is the explicit exception to its ordinary safe bedtime routine.
families.constraint: At most once per campaign after the player has bonded with the dog and learned night safety. Requires a validated short rescue route, pre-event checkpoint, bounded catch grace, and complete technical recovery logic.
